howToSteps.name: Rinse the filter
howToSteps.text: Fold the filter into the Chemex with the thick side on the spout. Rinse it well with hot water, then tip the rinse water away.

howToSteps.name: Add the coffee
howToSteps.text: Put 30 g of medium-coarse coffee in the filter for two mugs, or 47 g for a full 6-cup Chemex. Level the bed with a gentle shake.

howToSteps.name: Bloom, then pour
howToSteps.text: Pour about twice the coffee weight in water at 92 to 96 C and wait 30 seconds. Then pour the rest in slow circles.

howToSteps.name: Let it drain
howToSteps.text: The brew should finish in four to five minutes. Lift the filter out as soon as the dripping stops, give the pot a swirl, and serve.

lede: Chemex starts at 1:16, one gram of coffee for every 16 grams of water. That is 30 g of coffee to 480 g of water for two mugs, brewed through the thick Chemex filter.

title: Chemex Coffee to Water Ratio Guide
tutorial: Chemex is pour-over with a thicker filter, and the filter changes the cup. It holds back more oil and fine sediment, so the coffee comes out cleaner and lighter than the same beans in a V60. The ratio is the same starting point: 1:16, which is 30 g of coffee to 480 g of water for two mugs.

The thick filter also slows the drawdown, so a Chemex brew runs four to five minutes instead of three. Some roasters open the ratio to 1:17 to keep a long brew from over-extracting. Start at 1:16 and try 1:17 if the cup tastes heavy or bitter.

Grind a step coarser than you would for a V60: medium-coarse, like coarse sand. A fine grind in a Chemex stalls the drawdown and the bed floods. Rinse the filter well with hot water first, or the cup tastes like paper.

The 6-cup Chemex is the one most kitchens have, and it takes about 750 g of water with room for the bloom, which is 47 g of coffee at 1:16. Do not brew less than 30 g in it: a thin bed of grounds drains unevenly and the small batch tastes worse than a full one.

Pour in slow circles and keep the water level below the top of the filter. The bloom takes 30 seconds, then the main pour, then let it drain. The whole brew should finish in four to five minutes. Lift the filter out as soon as it stops dripping so the last bitter drops stay out of the pot.
